subject.title: fix(marketplaces): allow trusted feed key rotation

question: May an accepted signed-feed monotonic record be treated as authoritative for rollback comparison after the configured signing key set no longer verifies the previous envelope?
rationale: This choice defines the marketplace rollback trust boundary: requiring the replacement key to verify historical envelopes blocks legitimate rotation, while trusting persisted metadata is safe only if every write path proves prior signature acceptance.

options.title: Confirm metadata authority
options.body: Confirm the accepted monotonic record is written only after full signed-feed verification, add real persisted-store proof, and merge this narrow fix.

options.title: Require overlapping keys
options.body: Keep historical-envelope re-verification and require publishers to retain old and new trusted keys during a rotation window.

options.title: Pause trust rollout
options.body: Hold this PR and the dependent default-feed trust work until a different authenticated rollback-record design is agreed.

recommendation.title: Confirm metadata authority
recommendation.body: Confirm the accepted monotonic record is written only after full signed-feed verification, add real persisted-store proof, and merge this narrow fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest available end-to-end context across this patch and the paired feed-trust proposal, although a repository owner must provide final authority.
